record.title: The Guideline for Japanese Governments' Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI for the sake of Evolution and Innovation of Public Administration
record.original_title: 行政の進化と革新のための生成AIの調達・利活用に係るガイドライン
record.short_title: Japan generative AI procurement and use guideline (DS-920)
record.issuing_body: Executive Board of the Council for the Promotion of a Digital Society (Government of Japan); prepared by the Digital Agency with the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
record.summary: Government-wide rules for Japanese ministries on procuring and using generative AI, to promote its use and manage its risks together. Each ministry appoints a Chief AI Officer (CAIO), who with the planners assesses each use case on four risk axes (who uses it, whether errors in the work could have serious effects, whether confidential or personal data are stored or learned, whether staff judge the output) and reports likely high-risk uses to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board, served by the Digital Agency and AISI. Procurement and contract check sheets set vendor requirements, and risk cases particular to generative AI must be handled and reported.
record.notes: Decided in writing at the 19th meeting of the Executive Board of the Council for the Promotion of a Digital Society on 27 May 2025, as Normative document DS-920 of the Digital Society Promotion Standard Guidelines; the Digital Agency prepared it with METI, MIC and other ministries. It replaced the government's agreement on business use of generative AI such as ChatGPT (version 2.1). Under the first edition it applied in full to generative AI systems procured or used from fiscal year 2026 (including planning and procurement steps before the end of March 2026), with best efforts in fiscal year 2025, and the governance framework of section 4 started in fiscal year 2025. Systems handling specially designated secrets, important economic security information, classified documents or sensitive security and public-order information are excluded; incorporated administrative agencies are expected to follow it and local governments may refer to it. A revised edition (version 2.0), approved on 12 June 2026, widens the scope from text-generating AI to generative AI that takes text and audio as input and produces text, images or audio, places systems that take images or video as input, generate video or perform advanced tasks such as AI agents under its governance framework, revises the high-risk criteria, adds examples of reportable risk cases and came into effect on 1 September 2026, with CAIO measures due by 30 June 2026 and the wider governance scope applying from 1 July 2026.

verification.note: Stored on 14 Oct 2026 from digital.go.jp: the Digital Agency's announcement page of 27 May 2025 (last updated 13 Jun 2025), which says it no longer shows the latest version; the Japanese text of the first edition (27 May 2025) and the Agency's provisional English translation of it; the Digital Society Promotion Standard Guidelines page, which lists DS-920 as Normative with last revision on 12 Jun 2026; and the Agency's provisional English translation of the revised edition of 12 Jun 2026. The Japanese text of the revised edition is not among the stored files: the summary is written from the Japanese first edition, and the account of the 2026 revision in the notes, including the effective date of 1 Sep 2026, rests on the provisional English translation. The English title follows the Agency's own provisional translation as named on its pages (the 2026 translation's cover reads 'Japanese Government's'). A further stored file (DS-202, a technical report on CI/CD pipeline security) is unrelated to this instrument.

judgment.status_reasoning: The first edition (27 May 2025) applies in full to generative AI systems procured or used from fiscal year 2026 (from April 2026), with section 4 from fiscal year 2025 (sec. 2.2.4); today (14 Oct 2026) is in fiscal year 2026. The standard guidelines page lists DS-920 as a current Normative document last revised on 12 Jun 2026, and the provisional English translation of that revision says it came into effect on 1 Sep 2026, which has passed. So: In force.
judgment.legal_force_reasoning: DS-920 is a Normative standard guideline: the document defines itself as rules to be complied with for the development and management of government information systems, and users must follow the rules each ministry's CAIO sets under it. It binds central government bodies as an internal government rule, not the public; recorded as Binding on that basis, as instrument type Guidelines / framework because it is issued as a guideline.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the decision of the Executive Board on 27 May 2025 (first edition); date_last_updated is the revision of 12 Jun 2026 (version 2.0). date_in_force is left null because the first edition sets application by fiscal year rather than an entry-into-force date, and the effective date of the revised edition (1 Sep 2026) is in the provisional English translation only and would misdate the instrument's original application; both are in the notes.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A government risk-management framework for public-sector use of generative AI, with risk assessment, a high-risk reporting duty, a governance body and incident handling: in scope with no note under AGENTS.md section 10 (government safety and risk-management frameworks and guidelines).

open_questions: date_in_force is null: the first edition sets application by fiscal year (in full for systems procured or used from FY2026, governance framework from FY2025) and the revised edition says it came into effect on 1 Sep 2026 (provisional English translation only). A human may prefer one of these dates.

The Japanese text of the revised edition of 12 Jun 2026 (DS-920 本文 on the standard guidelines page) is not stored; the summary describes the first edition, and the notes' account of the 2026 revision rests on the provisional English translation.
